chunks: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal narrated to us from his father from Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Musa al-Rida from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

Surely, the month of Ramadan is a great month. In it, Allah multiplies good deeds, erases sins, and uplifts ranks. Whoever gives charity in this month, Allah will forgive him. Whoever is good to his slave in it, Allah will forgive him. Whoever beautifies his character in it, Allah will forgive him. Whoever withholds his anger in it, Allah will forgive him. Whoever maintains family ties in it, Allah will forgive him.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: Surely, this month of yours is not like the other months. When it comes to you, it comes with blessing and mercy; and when it leaves you, it leaves with the forgiveness of sins. This is the month of good deeds multiplied in it, and good actions in it are accepted. Whoever among you prays two voluntary units for Allah the Mighty and Majestic in this month, Allah will forgive him. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Surely, the truly wretched one is he who leaves this month without his sins being forgiven. Then he will lose, while the righteous win the rewards of the Generous Lord.

key_terms.الشقي حق الشقي: The truly wretched — an emphatic construction meaning the most truly unfortunate person
key_terms.ما ملكت يمينه: What his right hand possesses — a reference to servants or dependents
key_terms.يضاعف الحسنات: Multiplies good deeds — each righteous act is counted manifold during Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What virtues and rewards of Ramadan does the Prophet Muhammad describe?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, transmitted through the golden chain of Imam al-Rida and narrated at the first Friday assembly of Ramadan 367 AH, describes the unparalleled virtues of the month of Ramadan. Five acts of worship are enumerated — charity, kindness to dependents, good character, controlling anger, and maintaining family ties — each of which earns forgiveness. The Prophet's words emphasize that Ramadan is unlike any other month, arriving with blessing and departing with forgiveness, and that the truly unfortunate person is one who lets this opportunity pass unforgiven.
